newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude rises, physical swaps up on margins.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude rises, physical swaps up on margins.

text.p: Brent crude rose on the paper market on Monday with CFDs also tightening on a more bullish tone to the physical market, bolstered talk of improved refining margins, traders said.
The Brent cash market rose sharply, trading 37 cents higher at $18.29 a barrel by 1230 GMT.
Traders said that on the North Sea physical market, a Statfjord cargo was sold but details were not immediately available.
Although the was quiet, both intermonth spreads and CFDs firmed further.
May/June and June/July remained steady at -20 cents and -11 cents levels respectively, while July/August fetched -11, or two cents firmer from its early trade level.
CFDs rose with next week's dates trading at June Brent -39 while May 5-9 was two cents stronger at June Brent -37 cents.
"The market is doing fine and I think premiums are picking up and things are getting fantastic, I mean fantastic for producers," one trader said.
The positive sentiment was "because of the refining margins, the improvement in refining margins," he added. "CFDs are firmer, even from early this morning."
"The market in general is better bid than the CFD market," the trader said.

Others said the North Sea market could get a shot in the arm from the opportunity to substitute for West African barrels in the U.S. Gulf, as millions of barrels of Nigerian and other West African grades were heading to Asia.

The West African market was quiet but traders said that last week's flurry of activity, with Nigerian and other grades being picked up by Japanese, South Korean and Chinese buyers, has pushed up spot differentials.
"There's not too many unsold (West African) cargoes left out there. There's a fair number but not that much left," one trader said.
"Anyone wanting to buy West African grades would have to pay highter prices," he said, adding that differrentials for some Nigerian grades were in the Dated Brent +30/+40 cents region.

In a quiet Mediterranean market, Russian Urals was a little weaker than last week's levels, being talked at about Dated Brent -$1.20 cif, with looming pressure from cheaper grades, namely Iraq's Kirkuk, in May.
Negotiations between Syrian state oil company Sytrol and term lifters over May term prices were expected to end later this weak, traders said.
The Syrians were insisting on their offer of Dated Brent -82 cents while buyers were hoping to pay the mid-80s range, they said.
A rollover of the April prices of Dated Brent -95 cents for Syrian Light seemed difficult as some buyers were prepared to pay as high as Brent -92 cents.
